labs.title: Louise Sloan 5:1 Optotype Waterfall
labs.mystery: Traditional eye charts made some letters 40% easier to guess than others. Ten specific letters solved this in 1959 by locking to a single mathematical ratio. Can you find why a 1-arcminute stroke matters at 55 cm?
mission: Find the Waterfall stage at the top of the broadside.
Observe the 10 definitive Sloan characters: C, D, H, K, N, O, R, S, V, Z.
Notice how the stroke width is exactly 1/5th of the total letter height.
labs.discovery: Snellen letters were unequal; Dr. Louise Sloan engineered 10 balanced optotypes where every letter shares identical psychometric legibility.

labs.title: Herman Bouma Lateral Crowding & Anti-Masking
labs.mystery: When your fovea focuses straight ahead, letters in your peripheral vision don't blur—they crowd together into unrecognizable shapes. What critical distance breaks this visual trap?
mission: In the waterfall stage, locate the tracking and lateral spacing metrics.
Observe how Bouma's constant (r ≈ 0.5 × eccentricity) governs the +0.12em lateral clearance.
Compare dense character packing against Bouma-spaced clinical alert numbers.
labs.discovery: Adding +0.12em lateral tracking creates spatial isolation, allowing nurses and surgeons to read vital numbers in their peripheral vision without turning their heads.

labs.title: Slashed Zero vs Capital O (cv08)
labs.mystery: On a smudged ICU touchscreen, a single circular character can mean either an oxygen saturation reading or a patient's room letter. One diagonal line saves lives.
mission: Scroll to Section 3: ISMP Clinical Disambiguation.
Click the '0 vs O' inspection card.
Observe the internal 45° diagonal slash and optical thinning at the junctions.
labs.discovery: Feature cv08 provides a crisp diagonal slash that never clots with ink or pixels, completely eliminating 0 vs O confusion in critical dosages like 500 mg.

labs.title: Philocardia Hearts & 72 BPM Cardiac Pacing

location.label: Section 3.5 • Philocardia Live Heart Tittle Studio

labs.mystery: Typefaces are usually cold and clinical metal. But can a font breathe at the exact resting heart rate of a child, and turn punctuation into lovingkindness?
mission: Locate the Philocardia Healer Banner with the beating green heart.
Click the '72 BPM', '60 BPM', and 'Static' cadence buttons to feel the pacing shift.
Click into the live text editor and type lowercase 'i', 'j', or '!' to witness procedural heart tittles.
labs.discovery: Features cv09 and ss07 replace standard square dots with humanist felt-marker hearts, paced to parasympathetic heart cadences (60–72 BPM) for pediatric comfort.

labs.title: 650nm Scotopic Night-Shift Observatory Console
labs.mystery: A single flash of white light at an observatory destroys 30 minutes of deep-sky dark adaptation. How can astronomers read celestial coordinates without bleaching their rhodopsin?
mission: Navigate to Section 5.1 in the Scientific Lab.
Click the button 'Activate 650nm Scotopic Red Mode'.
Watch the entire console shift into monochromatic deep-red photons (>650nm).
labs.discovery: Light above 650nm bypasses retinal rod photopigments, preserving night vision at mountaintop observatories and sleep cycles during clinician night shifts.

labs.title: The 118-Element IUPAC Periodic Table
labs.mystery: 118 elements form the entire universe. Why does each element tile sit in an encapsulated dark chassis even when the website is set to cream paper or bright white?
mission: Scroll to Section 5.2: The Standard 118-Element Periodic Table.
Click Element 8 (Oxygen, O) or Element 26 (Iron, Fe).
Toggle through the Daltonism filters (Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Monochromacy) to test legibility.
labs.discovery: The dark chassis protects vibrant CPK chemical tokens from photopic washout on white backgrounds, maintaining >15:1 WCAG AAA contrast in all lighting conditions.

labs.title: UNDRIP Accord & Pan-Tribal Typography

location.label: Chapter 7 • Global Health Atlas & World Scripts

labs.mystery: Many fonts force Indigenous languages into Latin metal boxes or clip their stacked high-tone nasal marks. Which international human rights accord guarantees typographic linguistic sovereignty?
mission: Visit the Global Health Atlas and World Scripts stage.
Inspect the Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics and Lushootseed Salishan orthographies.
Observe how stacked nasal marks (ą́, ę́, į́, ǫ́) maintain ≥ 110 UPM clearance without clipping.
labs.discovery: Conforming to UNDRIP Articles 11, 13, 14, 24, and 31, PocketGull guarantees unencumbered SIL OFL 1.1 open licensing and zero forced Latinization for tribal immersion schools.

labs.title: Full 256 Unicode Braille ISO/TR 11548 Matrix
labs.mystery: Can a digital font on a glass screen simultaneously honor the physical geometry of an embossing pin on cardstock?
mission: Locate the Braille Studio or tactile strip in ICU Telemetry.
Type any clinical dosage or phrase in the transcriber.
Inspect the 2.5 mm dot pitch and baseline grounding on y = 0.
labs.discovery: PocketGull maps all 256 Unicode Braille codepoints (U+2800–U+28FF) with zero .notdef missing glyphs, matching international ISO/TR 11548 tactile standards.

labs.title: 88-Key Stretched Rainbow Piano & Chromatic Pedagogy
labs.mystery: How do visual light wavelengths (ROYGBIV) map directly to acoustic sound frequencies across a grand piano?
mission: Scroll to Chapter 6: GearArts Physical Atelier.
Explore the 88-Key Stretched Rainbow Piano.
Click keys to hear WebAudio synthesized harmonics and observe chromatic octave tokens.
labs.discovery: Chromatic note tokens bridge ophthalmological optics and auditory music theory, helping neurodivergent learners intuitively perceive pitch intervals through color.

labs.title: Thomas Phinney Forensic 2-Byte Alignment & OTS Safety
labs.mystery: Why do some fonts work for one second in Chromium and then silently vanish from memory? A single odd number in an offset table causes silent font eviction.
mission: Scroll to the Downloads & Foundry Governance section.
Review the 7 Invariant Quality Pillars.
Notice the mathematical rule: loca[i] % 2 == 0 across all 32 font cuts.
labs.discovery: DirectWrite and Chromium OTS evict fonts with odd table offsets. PocketGull pads every single glyph record to even 2-byte word boundaries for 100% memory safety.
